evidence: Row only asserts, in the shared loop: `assert verdict["signature"]["signed"] is False, f"{label} must not sign"` (line 1653) — no verdict-class or coverage assertion for the outage row

Existing tests establish the outage seam yields INDETERMINATE, not degraded: `assert v["verdict"] == "INDETERMINATE" and not v["signature"]["signed"]` / `assert v["coverage"].get("llm_unavailable") is True` (lines 628-630)

advisory.finding: The new 'degraded-outage' row in test_never_sign_guard_table asserts only `signed is False` and never asserts the verdict class it purports to exercise; because a runner raising LLMUnavailableError produces INDETERMINATE (llm_ran=False, llm_unavailable=True) — per the existing tests at lines 605-607 and 628-630 — the row is behaviorally indistinguishable from the 'not-claimable' INDETERMINATE row and adds no distinct regression coverage. A regression that let an outage sign (or that changed the outage verdict class) would only be caught by the generic `signed is False` check, not by any assertion specific to the degraded/outage path.
scenarios: An outage that regresses to sign or to a different verdict class than expected
